name: application-story-ring-row
title: Story Ring Row
description: A horizontal row of circular story avatars with a gradient ring for unseen stories, a muted ring for seen ones, and an add-story affordance, in a scrollable row and a compact preview cluster.
useWhen: Building an ephemeral-content feed (stories, status updates) where users need to see at a glance who has new content to view.
The list of contacts or contributors needs a compact, scrollable entry point into per-person detail views.
avoidWhen: You need a static group of avatars with no seen/unseen distinction or interaction — use an avatar group instead.
The content behind each avatar isn't ephemeral or story-like — a persistent feed is better served by a list or grid, not a ring row.
responsiveBehavior: The full row is a horizontally scrollable flex list (overflow-x-auto) so it degrades gracefully on narrow viewports without wrapping; the compact variant fits a fixed number of avatars plus an overflow count button.
accessibility: Each story's alt text states both who it belongs to and whether it has been seen, since that distinction is otherwise conveyed only by the ring's gradient vs. muted color.
The add-story control is a real <button> with an aria-label, since it contains only an icon.
The overflow '+N' button in the compact variant carries an aria-label describing exactly how many additional stories it reveals.

variants.title: Scrollable row
variants.description: Add-story button followed by unseen (gradient ring) and seen (muted ring) story avatars with name labels
accessibility: Alt text states both the person's name and seen/unseen status.

variants.title: Scrollable row (Dark)
variants.description: Add-story button followed by unseen (gradient ring) and seen (muted ring) story avatars with name labels
accessibility: Colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.

variants.title: Compact cluster
variants.description: Smaller unlabeled avatars with an overflow '+N' button, for a tighter header or sidebar context
accessibility: The overflow button's aria-label states exactly how many more stories it reveals.
